predecessors.name: Chavdas of Bhillamala
predecessors.text: the Chavdas of Bhillamala, whom Nagabhata I may originally have served as a feudatory (infobox Predecessors)

successors.name: Gahadavala dynasty
successors.text: Chandradeva founded the Gahadavala dynasty with its capital at Kannauj 'around 1090' (Kannauj page)

capitals.name: Bari (across the Ganges east of Kannauj)

ledger.x: 730: Nagabhata I founds the Pratihara state, reaching out from Mandor and taking Avanti (Ujjain) as capital.
738: Nagabhata I leads a confederacy against the Arabs.
743: the Arabs have lost their Rajasthan and Gujarat conquests.
750: Cliopatria's Pratihara shape grows by about 0.25 M km2 (Gujarat, more of Malwa, part of Bundelkhand).
750: Dantidurga's hold on Malwa and southern Gujarat meets the Pratihara shape.
756: Dantidurga's reign ends.
772: Cliopatria's shape grows again (Gwalior side, Bundelkhand, Rajasthan), the year before Vatsaraja's reign on the page (775-805, 'master of western quarter'); no page dates the land.
783: Cliopatria's shape reaches its maximum before 788.
785: Vatsaraja takes the submission of Kannauj.

c. 786: Dhruva of the Rashtrakutas crosses the Narmada into Malwa and tries to take Kannauj. The page: c. 786: Rashtrakuta ruler Dhruva crossed the Narmada into Malwa and tried to take Kannauj; the Tripartite page has him defeat Vatsaraja, who flees to the Maru deserts, and then Dharmapala in the Doab, and notes he…
788: the eastern part of Cliopatria's 783 growth leaves the shape, about 137,000 km2 (the 783 gain below carried it as 'Bundelkhand and Gwalior' only).
790: Dhruva goes home.

c. 791: Dharmapala of the Palas takes Kannauj out of Pratihara overlordship. The page: Dharmapala invades Kannauj 'around 791', defeats Indrayudha and installs his brother Chakrayudha as a vassal; a footnote says the events 'may be assigned to about 791 A.D.'. Kannauj is not annexed.
800: Govinda III's northern campaign.

c. 806: Lata passes to the Rashtrakutas. The page: Govinda III took Malwa, Lata, and Mahakoshal from the Gurjaras, undated between 793 and 814; Cliopatria's shape loses southern Gujarat in 806, and the Rashtrakuta page has him 'took firm hold over Gujarat'. Malwa is regained under Nagabhata II, so…
814: Govinda III dies and the Rashtrakuta threat ends.
816: Nagabhata II takes Kannauj.
816: the Pratihara capital moves from Avanti (Ujjain) to Kannauj; the page makes Kannauj the Pratihara capital with the 816 victory.
836 and the years after: the Chandelas of Bundelkhand acknowledge Mihira Bhoja.
842: Mihira Bhoja drives the Arabs out of Kutch.
860: Bhoja's Gujarat, as Cliopatria draws it.
860: Cliopatria's Pratihara shape holds 16% of Sindh from 860, overlapping its Habbari shape.
914: Saurashtra under Pratihara suzerainty.

c. 916: Indra III of the Rashtrakutas sacks Kannauj. The page: c. 916: Indra III sacked Kannauj. The Pratiharas later regained the city. The Indra III page says Kannauj was 'completely destroyed', Mahipala I fled 'as if struck by lightning', and the Rashtrakutas 'were actually able to hold Kannauj until c. 916'; the…
926: Kannauj is back in Pratihara hands.
936: Malwa passes to the Paramaras.
936: the Sindh part of the shape is dropped.
942: Gujarat and Kutch leave the Pratihara map when Mularaja founds the Chaulukya state.

c. 942: Saurashtra leaves the Pratihara tint when Mularaja overthrows the last Chavda king and defeats Graharipu of Saurashtra. The Chavdas of Vardhamana are not said to fall in 942, and the Saindhava page ends the Saindhavas between 920 and 987 and has a 987 inscription of a…
947: about 25,000 km2 of southern Rajasthan and the Gujarat border leave Cliopatria's shape, all of it inside Cliopatria's Chaulukya shape that begins in 947.

c. 950: the Chandelas stop acknowledging the Pratiharas. The Chandela page: Yashovarman (c. 925-950) 'continued to acknowledge the Pratihara suzerainty, but became practically independent'; Dhanga (c. 950-999) mentions no Pratihara overlord, 'This indicates that Dhanga formally established the Chandela sovereignty.'…
c. 950: the Chandelas take Gwalior. The Pratihara page: 'the Chandelas captured the strategic fortress of Gwalior in central India around 950.' Bundelkhand is not part of this loss in…
960: Rajasthan is in the hands of its former feudatories.
960: what is left of Malwa goes to the Paramaras (see 936).
1018: Mahmud of Ghazni marches on Kannauj.
1019: the Pratihara seat moves to Bari.
1019: the Pratihara state shrinks from the Doab to Cliopatria's rump round Kannauj plus Bari.
January 1019: Mahmud turns back to Ghazni after the battle at Sharwa on 6 January.
1036: Jasapala, the last Pratihara ruler of Kannauj, dies.

wars.name: Arab campaigns in Rajasthan and Gujarat
wars.outcome: Junayd (723-726) 'recaptured Sindh, conquered Gujarat and parts of Rajasthan' but not Ujjain; the Arabs 'lost their conquests in Rajasthan and Gujarat by 743'; the Chalukya general Pulakeshin defeated them at Navsari in 739; al-Hakam died fighting in 740.

wars.name: Dantidurga's subjugation of the Avanti Pratiharas
wars.outcome: The Dantidurga page says 'By 750 AD Dantidurga had brought Madhya Pradesh and Southern Gujarat under his control' and that he defeated the kings of Lata, Malwa and others (undated); the Tripartite Struggle page has him subdue a Pratihara king of Avanti, who…

wars.name: Tripartite Struggle
wars.outcome: Pratihara victory in 816: Nagabhata II defeats Chakrayudha and proclaims himself king of Kannauj; before that Vatsaraja (overlord), Dhruva (raid, home in 790), Dharmapala (Chakrayudha as Pala vassal c.

wars.name: Bhoja's wars against the Arabs of Sind
wars.outcome: Bhoja evicted the Arabs from Sindan and pushed them out of Kutch.

wars.name: Battle of Ujjain (Krishna II and Bhoja)
wars.outcome: Krishna II defeated the Pratiharas at Ujjain: 'Around 880' in one passage, 'Sometime before 888' in another.

wars.name: Indra III's invasion of the doab
Ghaznavid conquest of Kannauj
wars.outcome: Mahmud reaches Kannauj on 20 December 1018, Rajyapala flees to Bari, the city is plundered and left under local rulers; Mahmud is at Sharwa on 6 January 1019.

wars.name: Ghaznavid campaigns against Trilochanpala and Vidyadhara
wars.outcome: October 1020: Trilochanpala beaten at the Ramganga, Bari razed; 1022 Gwalior surrenders and Vidyadhara pays tribute and keeps fifteen fortresses.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line; the Narmada is the one river frontier the pages name ('the Narmada River in the south' in Bhoja's reign).
A Kannauj rump under Ghaznavid pressure; no frontier is described.
